title: Reduce complete positive-frame replay time by 71.4% (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Measured verifier improvement with a scoped equivalence proof and finite conformance evidence. An exact integer subset join reduces the complete positive-frame replay's median elapsed time by **71.4%**, from **29.031 s to 8.290 s**, in five alternating fresh-process pairs. All ten commands emit identical complete output with zero errors. No new kappa is claimed.

```text
original: construct every rational six-label subset sum
new:      clear all label and target denominators
          join four-label and two-label integer subset sets
          retain the complete split inventory and all other checks
```

Only `research/positive-frame-subset-join/` is added. Its adapter authenticates Josie Elliston's frozen PR #6111 checker and replaces one concrete support calculation in a fresh module. The proof covers repeated labels, signed coordinates, zero counts and different target denominators. The predecessor retains its theorem, checker, inventory and controls.

## Evidence

- Five complete baseline commands take **28.521–30.837 s**, median **29.031 s**; five accelerated commands take **8.190–8.394 s**, median **8.290 s**. CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, 18-core shared host. Timing includes startup, source authentication, every check, output and exit. Generated `BENCHMARK.json` binds the code and records every return code and output hash.
- A separate cProfile run places 84.219 of 102.461 instrumented seconds in the concrete scan, dominated by Fraction operations. Instrumented times are excluded from the comparison.
- All four target decisions on **46,916 concrete splits** agree with a separately written literal Fraction enumeration. The new verifier also checks **420** small rational cases and **seven** input/source rejections, then runs the complete accelerated source command. These are accelerator-conformance cases, not a new predecessor census.
- Direct warning-strict normal and optimized checks pass in **31.33 s** and **32.96 s**. Both registered commands pass; the registered invocation takes **65.21 s**. Each check is below its 300-second timeout.
- Metadata, AST parsing, exact committed bytes/modes and source-history ancestry pass at `3d452329bf4e4893c0a5205eecd61c3cd6c39cb4`. Official export integrity and an optimized read-only, Git-free replay with empty executable PATH pass. That replay takes **32.45 s** and preserves all 16 exported files, including the manifest. Export SHA256: `2c0ffa5370ce7f829f5a0d617eb1b3418bdf20200f7cb16c55c0cbecfd10d168`.

From the repository root, with the standard library:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/positive-frame-subset-join/run.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/positive-frame-subset-join/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/positive-frame-subset-join/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/positive-frame-subset-join
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/positive-frame-subset-join --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 installation may replace the interpreter path. Expected marker: `PASS_POSITIVE_FRAME_SUBSET_JOIN_CONFORMANCE no_new_kappa`. Add `--baseline` to run.py for original predicates. Optional timing reproduction:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/positive-frame-subset-join/benchmark.py --pairs 5 --output /tmp/positive-frame-benchmark.json
```

## Limitations and unrun obligations

This is a single-host measurement and a scoped equivalence result for the exact pinned checker. Unknown source revisions reject. Generic inputs have six rational triples, four targets, total multiplicity at most eight and explicit bit bounds. Managed-allocation and fixed authenticated module-execution deviations are recorded in PROOF.md.

No new positive-frame theorem, native word, supplier, multiplication bound or selected-frontier change is supplied. Native/compiler/ownership/precision/analytic admission, selected scientific cold replay, Lean and Docker were outside scope and were not run. Every registered local command passed. The predecessor's scientific review status is inherited; independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

Can a separate integer formulation reduce the unchanged symbolic support-classification stage? First profile the complete accelerated command and specify that stage's exact return-value contract. No implementation, measured gain or follow-on reservation is included here.

## Related open work

Completion refresh on 2026-10-29 inspected all 13 other open account PRs created since the advance CLAIM at 13:10:51 UTC. None studies this exact checker or added-positive-frame endpoint, changes its implementation, or supplies a competing result. No conflicting number was found and no extra mathematical computations were run.

Adjacent performance work has separate commands and workloads:

- #6177 reduces complete replay-planning time. Its planner measurement is separate from this scientific-checker measurement; no gains are combined.
- #6179 reduces current task-picker startup time. It changes a different entry point and supplies no competing checker result.

The earlier refreshed 330-PR snapshot and immediate precommit query for #6111 also found no same-object open work. Merged #6111 is the source workload; merged #6148 and #6158 study separate mathematical extensions and are not replayed or extended here.

Base and refreshed main are `3f0152a32eeebac0df11946dbd50cabe5a7f7839`, priority revision 8. Live claims, reservations, recent account work, main README terms and merged searches were checked. Remote overlap pagination was complete; sparse local-note coverage was incomplete. This is bounded coordination evidence.

## Credit

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Josie Elliston's #6111 for the theorem, source checker, split inventory and controls; JoyboyBrian's #6104 for the two-frame question and parameterization; apoursh's #6089 for the classification and symmetries; Cinna Davis for the PR2085/2112 model; Philippe Van Velzen for the earlier floor; Nick Petalas for the determinant method; and the retained BIT/formal-model lineage. Denominator clearing and subset joining are standard techniques. The new work is their source-bound integration, equivalence argument and complete-command evidence. Predecessor notices are unchanged. Apache-2.0.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19267812).

## CI notes

Both hosted checks **passed** at `3d452329bf4e4893c0a5205eecd61c3cd6c39cb4` in [Registered research packages run 40883034303](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40883034303). The `plan` check passed in 4m43s and `replay (research/positive-frame-subset-join)` passed in 5m24s. This certifies the registered normal/optimized conformance replay at the published head. All listed local checks also passed.

Hosted conformance does not certify the local performance percentage or provide independent human or formal proof-kernel acceptance. No code changed after these checks.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: package. One isolated opt-in package is added; shared code, frozen inputs and the selected result are unchanged.
